finding_title: Street tree canopy associated with lower perceived heat stress
finding_description: Hypothetical field measurements in two neighbourhoods suggest lower surface temperatures and lower perceived heat stress at pedestrian level under mature tree canopy than on comparable unshaded streets.
evidence_limitation: Two neighbourhoods and one summer season only; results may not transfer to other climates, street layouts or tree species.

finding_title: Cooling effect depends on street geometry
finding_description: Hypothetical microclimate simulations suggest that dense canopy in narrow streets may reduce daytime heat but slow night-time cooling, so the net effect varies with street width and orientation.
evidence_limitation: Simulation results were not validated against night-time measurements; model assumptions are simplified.

finding_title: Newly planted trees provide limited shade in early years
finding_description: Hypothetical planting records indicate that young street trees provide little shade during their first years, delaying expected cooling benefits.
evidence_limitation: Based on planting records from a single fictional municipality; growth rates vary by species and site.

finding_title: Green roofs reduce peak indoor temperatures in top-floor dwellings
finding_description: Hypothetical monitoring of pilot buildings suggests lower peak indoor temperatures in top-floor dwellings beneath green roofs than beneath conventional roofs.
evidence_limitation: Small sample of poorly insulated buildings; effect may be smaller in well-insulated or newer buildings.

finding_title: Green roofs retain part of rainfall from moderate events
finding_description: Hypothetical monitoring suggests green roofs retain a meaningful share of rainfall during moderate events, but retention falls sharply during intense or prolonged storms once the substrate is saturated.
evidence_limitation: Extreme rainfall events were rare during the monitoring period and are under-represented in the data.

finding_title: Roof vegetation may require irrigation in dry summers
finding_description: Hypothetical case observations indicate that some green roofs needed irrigation during dry summers to keep vegetation alive, creating a possible tension with water-saving objectives.
evidence_limitation: Observations from a small number of buildings in one fictional climate zone; drought-tolerant planting was not tested.

finding_title: Floodplain restoration lowers modelled downstream peak levels
finding_description: Hypothetical hydrological modelling suggests that restoring upstream floodplains could reduce peak water levels in a downstream urban area during design flood scenarios.
evidence_limitation: Hypothetical catchment; model uncertainty was not quantified and results depend on land availability assumptions.

finding_title: Retention capacity of small urban parks varies with soil conditions
finding_description: Hypothetical infiltration tests suggest that the water retention capacity of small urban parks varies considerably with soil type and compaction, so similar designs may perform differently.
evidence_limitation: Soil sampling at a limited number of sites; seasonal variation not assessed.

finding_title: Residents value multi-functional retention areas
finding_description: Hypothetical survey responses suggest residents value retention areas that also serve as recreational green space, which may support local acceptance.
evidence_limitation: Self-reported views from a non-random sample; acceptance may differ where land use conflicts exist.

finding_title: Reflective pavements lower surface temperatures
finding_description: Hypothetical measurements suggest that reflective pavement coatings reduce road surface temperatures compared with conventional asphalt on hot days.
evidence_limitation: Surface temperature only; pedestrian thermal comfort was not measured. Coating durability not assessed.

finding_title: Reflected radiation may increase pedestrian heat exposure
finding_description: Hypothetical modelling suggests that highly reflective ground surfaces could increase the radiation reaching pedestrians, partly offsetting lower surface temperatures.
evidence_limitation: Model-based result that appears to be in tension with surface-temperature measurements; requires field validation.

finding_title: Maintenance budgets often not planned at installation
finding_description: Hypothetical interviews with municipal staff suggest that long-term maintenance costs of urban vegetation are frequently not budgeted when green infrastructure is first installed.
evidence_limitation: Small number of interviews in fictional municipalities; may not represent practice elsewhere.

finding_title: Vegetation losses linked to drought and limited maintenance
finding_description: Hypothetical site inspections associate higher vegetation losses with drought periods combined with limited watering and care.
evidence_limitation: Observational association only; other causes such as soil quality or vandalism were not systematically recorded.

finding_title: Upfront costs higher for nature-based measures in dense areas
finding_description: Hypothetical cost analysis suggests that nature-based measures may have higher upfront costs in dense urban areas because of land and retrofitting constraints.
evidence_limitation: Based on illustrative price assumptions; co-benefits such as recreation or biodiversity were not monetised.

finding_title: Lifecycle cost comparison sensitive to assumptions
finding_description: Hypothetical lifecycle cost comparison of nature-based and engineered drainage options suggests that the preferred option changes depending on the discount rate and assumed maintenance costs.
evidence_limitation: Results are highly sensitive to assumptions; no single option is consistently cheaper across scenarios.

finding_title: Fragmented responsibilities may delay implementation
finding_description: Hypothetical case studies suggest that adaptation measures are delayed where responsibilities for water, green space and roads sit with separate departments without a coordinating mechanism.
evidence_limitation: Three fictional cities only; administrative structures vary widely between Member States.

finding_title: Adaptation plans rarely include monitoring indicators
finding_description: Hypothetical document review suggests that few of the sampled local adaptation plans define indicators for monitoring whether measures achieve their objectives.
evidence_limitation: Review of plan documents only; monitoring may take place without being documented in plans.

finding_title: Heat alerts may not reach all vulnerable residents
finding_description: Hypothetical survey results suggest that local heat-alert schemes reached fewer older and socially isolated residents than intended.
evidence_limitation: Survey responses may under-represent the most isolated residents, who are hardest to reach.

finding_title: Participatory mapping associated with higher flood risk awareness
finding_description: Hypothetical before-and-after comparison suggests that residents who took part in participatory flood risk mapping reported higher awareness of local flood risk.
evidence_limitation: Short follow-up period and self-selected participants; no evidence on changes in behaviour.

finding_title: Protected cycle lanes associated with higher cycling counts
finding_description: Hypothetical automatic counts suggest more cycling trips on corridors after protected lanes were introduced than before.
evidence_limitation: Before-and-after comparison without a control corridor; part of the increase may reflect trips diverted from parallel streets.

finding_title: Increase in cycling partly driven by existing cyclists
finding_description: Hypothetical survey responses suggest that a substantial share of additional trips were made by people who already cycled, so the shift away from car use may be smaller than counts imply.
evidence_limitation: Self-reported travel behaviour; non-random sample of corridor users.

finding_title: Initial business concerns eased after implementation
finding_description: Hypothetical interviews suggest that local retailers who opposed the cycle lanes before construction reported fewer concerns one year later.
evidence_limitation: Small number of retrospective interviews; retailers who closed or relocated were not included.

finding_title: E-scooter trips mostly replace walking and public transport
finding_description: Hypothetical survey data suggest that most shared e-scooter trips replace walking or public transport rather than car trips, limiting expected emission reductions.
evidence_limitation: Single city and single season; replacement patterns may differ in cities with lower public transport provision.

finding_title: Designated parking reduced pavement obstruction complaints
finding_description: Hypothetical case data suggest fewer complaints about obstructed pavements after dedicated e-scooter parking zones were introduced.
evidence_limitation: Complaint records are an indirect measure; enforcement changed at the same time.

finding_title: Shared e-scooter use concentrated in central districts
finding_description: Hypothetical trip records suggest that most rentals start and end in central districts, with limited use in outer neighbourhoods.
evidence_limitation: Data from one fictional operator; fleet distribution decisions by the operator influence observed demand.

finding_title: Electric buses lower modelled local air pollutant emissions
finding_description: Hypothetical route-level modelling suggests lower local emissions of air pollutants when diesel buses are replaced by electric buses.
evidence_limitation: Tailpipe emissions only; emissions from electricity generation and battery production were outside the model scope.

finding_title: Cold weather reduces electric bus range
finding_description: Hypothetical operational monitoring suggests reduced daily range in winter because of cabin heating, requiring additional vehicles or charging on some routes.
evidence_limitation: One winter season in one fictional climate; newer battery and heating technology may perform differently.

finding_title: Depot charging upgrades are a major cost driver
finding_description: Hypothetical cost analysis suggests that grid connection and depot upgrades account for a large share of fleet electrification costs.
evidence_limitation: Illustrative cost assumptions; grid connection costs vary strongly by location.

finding_title: On-demand services improved access in peri-urban areas
finding_description: Hypothetical case data suggest that demand-responsive minibuses improved access to services for residents without a car in low-density areas.
evidence_limitation: Short pilot period; novelty effects may inflate early use.

finding_title: Cost per passenger higher than for fixed-route buses
finding_description: Hypothetical cost analysis suggests that demand-responsive services have a higher operating cost per passenger than conventional fixed-route buses.
evidence_limitation: Social benefits of improved access were not valued; costs may fall as services mature.

finding_title: Low-income households report difficulty adapting to low-emission zones
finding_description: Hypothetical survey responses suggest that low-income households found it harder to replace non-compliant vehicles or change travel habits.
evidence_limitation: Self-reported difficulties; sample may over-represent people affected by the scheme.

finding_title: Support schemes associated with higher acceptance
finding_description: Hypothetical document review and case comparison suggest that low-emission zones accompanied by exemptions or financial support faced less public opposition.
evidence_limitation: Comparison of a few fictional schemes; other differences between cities may explain acceptance levels.

finding_title: Integrated mobility plans linked with faster delivery of cycling infrastructure
finding_description: Hypothetical case studies suggest that municipalities with an adopted integrated mobility plan delivered cycling infrastructure more quickly.
evidence_limitation: Association only; municipalities with plans may also have more resources and political support.

finding_title: Limited data sharing hampers monitoring of mobility measures
finding_description: Hypothetical interviews suggest that limited data sharing between transport operators and public authorities makes it difficult to monitor the effects of mobility measures.
evidence_limitation: Views of public authority staff only; operators' perspectives were not collected.
